title: Who answers the agents' permission requests?
context: Every permission prompt from every agent (bash commands, file edits and so on) goes to Matt today, which makes him the bottleneck. The idea was always that these reach the orchestrator, which answers them under authority Matt grants, while he watches and can review. Extends decision 7: push, merge and delete stay with Matt.

options.name: Orchestrator answers within rules Matt sets
options.summary: Requests go to the orchestrator first. A rules entry on the board says what it may allow (build, test, read, edits inside the project, local commits). Push, merge, delete, package installs, anything outside the project folder and network access always go to Matt. Every answer is logged in the orchestrator's thread, and Matt can change or revoke the rules at any time.
pros: Every answer is logged for audit
cons: The orchestrator may misjudge a borderline request

options.name: Fixed allowlist, no judgment
options.summary: The hub auto-approves anything matching a pattern list; the rest still goes to Matt.
cons: Every new command shape is another prompt

options.name: Orchestrator answers everything except a short block list
options.summary: Only push, merge, delete and work outside the project reach Matt.
cons: Installs and network access pass without Matt seeing them

recommendation: Removes almost all the bash prompts while keeping Matt in charge of anything hard to undo, with a log to audit. B can be added later as a fast path for obviously safe commands.

settles.value: orchestrator answers permission prompts within human-set rules; push, merge, delete, installs, outside-project and network always go to the human; every answer logged
